PROTOTYPE PLAN

IMPLEMENTATION / VALIDATE BEFORE EXPANDING

Agree on meaning.
Prove it survives failure.

Three proposed prototype sprints test whether Midnight Express can coordinate confidential work safely across different applications.

Start with quote coordination, prove durable recovery, then reuse the core for invoices and human-approved agents. Ten design reviews shaped this plan.

Proposed · no sprints completedTwo weeks each is a planning assumption

Staffing and start dates are not established. Gates determine whether to advance, revise scope or repeat work.

AVAILABLE NOW / CONFORMANCE & LOCAL PROTOTYPE

The reference is implemented.
The protocol gates stay visible.

Shared meaning, independently checked

Strict v0.2 contracts fix the review’s parsing and replay defects. Two declared price formats map to the same economics and complete intent. Independent interpreters agree on canonical bytes and safely refuse unsupported input.

Immutable contract bundles preserve meaning separately from implementation releases. The original v0.1 is retained as read-only history.

Failure evidence from a real database

Umbra’s public transaction API commits inbox, action, report, budget, outbox, checkpoint and cursor together on PostgreSQL. Process-kill tests recover one report write; uncertain destination acknowledgement waits for reconciliation.

These use synthetic authority and source evidence. The three protocol sprints remain proposed: genuine admission, signing, sealed-wire integration, live finality and customer baselines are still required.

Read implementation evidence ↗ in the private repository.

FIRST / SHARED MEANING

A small core.
Explicit workflow contracts.

A shared JSON format cannot tell a buyer whether a price is per share or per hundred shares. Each participant must agree to the same economic meaning.

Explore the dedicated Data Model guide →

One common mechanism

Private event identity, source, time and an exact contract commitment. Closed profiles define RFQ economics, invoice evidence and agent permissions independently. Deterministic adapters translate declared source conventions; missing units or roles cause rejection.

100 shares at $123.45 each means $12,345. A cents-per-hundred quote can agree only when its currency, denominator and perspective are explicitly declared.

Designed and reference-tested

The v0.2 reference has three closed event types and unsigned fixtures for quotes, payment observations and sandbox approvals. Strict parsing, expiry and occurrence/action conflicts are tested. Python, Rust and TypeScript agree on 35 RFQ vectors; two source-format adapters agree on the same complete fixture intent. Validation returns executes:false.

A separate Umbra/PostgreSQL sandbox passes 56 recovery checks, including four actual worker kills. Its effect is one database report row under fixture authority. Real authentication, consensus evidence and complete protocol integration remain gated.

Literature basis: Domain-Driven Design · CloudEvents · JSON Schema · FINOS CDM · UBL Invoice · JCS

APPLICATION DOMAINS / ETHEREUM & SOLANA

Common application events.
Chain-specific evidence.

The proposed domain covers the messages developers already consume, while keeping observation, intent and permission distinct.

Ethereum applications

RPC queries and results; blocks and reorgs; pending transactions and receipts; contract logs; balances and storage; ERC-20, ERC-721 and ERC-1155 transfers and approvals; wallet accounts, network changes and signing requests.

Safe and finalized remain Ethereum-specific assertions. Removed logs invalidate prior observations. Replacement and drop claims retain their inference policy; ABI and contract-version commitments identify decoded meaning.

Solana applications

RPC queries and results; slots, blocks and roots; account/program updates; transaction signatures and errors; instruction and CPI evidence; SOL and SPL/Token-2022 balances, transfers and authorities; wallet signing requests.

Processed, confirmed and finalized remain Solana-specific commitments. Preserve cluster identity, mint decimals, account owner and decoder version. Logs alone do not establish successful execution.

Shared coverage and implementation boundary

Simulation, fees, subscription lifecycle, gap/backfill, staking, governance, NFT, oracle, DeFi and bridge observations receive explicit domain families. Protocol-specific swaps, lending and bridge completion require separately pinned ABI/program contracts. Large RPC objects use bounded projections and evidence references. The corrected machine catalog records 291 proposed vocabulary entries. Separate read-only ERC-20 and legacy SPL projections pass 28 fixture checks for exact raw amounts, instruction outcomes, rollback and replay. The full vocabulary, live chain adapters and production execution contracts remain proposed.

SPRINT 01 / PROPOSED TWO-WEEK TIMEBOX

Agree on meaning. Exchange a quote.

Two independently specified participant formats can mean exactly the same trade, without guessed defaults.

What we build

  • Closed RFQ contract and two deterministic source adapters; independent Rust/TypeScript interpretation.
  • A buyer and two dealers on actual whole-shard GossipSub, with typed requests, offers and off-chain acceptance.
  • Start genuine admission and finalized Registry feasibility immediately; label any mock boundary.

What the demo must show

100 shares at 123.45 USD per share maps identically from two declared price conventions. An expired offer, wrong role or missing price basis fails.

Evidence required to advance
  • Equal canonical economics and intent commitments across implementations; ambiguous mappings reject.
  • Independent wire vectors; trace inspection finds no RFQ topics or upstream business selectors.
  • Candidate proof compatibility and actual encoded size/verification report, or a named blocking mismatch.

SPRINT 02 / PROPOSED TWO-WEEK TIMEBOX

Recover without changing the outcome.

The same accepted meaning and durable progress survive duplicate delivery, crashes and reconnect.

What we build

  • Compose authenticated inbox, dedup, local effect, outbox, checkpoint and cursor in one UmbraDB/PostgreSQL transaction.
  • Persistent opaque replay fixture, bounded retries, encrypted quarantine and explicit gap handling.
  • Carry pinned semantic contracts through restart and replay; continue proof, root and privacy checks.

What the demo must show

Kill the host before commit, after commit before acknowledgement and during outbox delivery. Replay and restore one accepted record, with no cursor beyond an uncommitted effect.

Evidence required to advance
  • Real process/crash fault matrix; same business action with a new EID cannot duplicate the effect.
  • Expired redrive, wrong restore context and unsupported contract cannot become actionable.
  • Paired recognition traces show no subscription-dependent acknowledgements or schema fetches.

SPRINT 03 / PROPOSED TWO-WEEK TIMEBOX

Reuse the core. Test the investment case.

Invoices and human-approved agents can reuse the core without a universal business schema or unsafe inferred authority.

What we build

  • Restricted invoice/payment observations with pending, partial, final and reversed evidence; no payment execution.
  • Separate proposal, approval, execution request and result contracts for one human-approved sandbox action.
  • Reuse fault harness and measure adapter effort; evaluate chain-domain profiles without treating indexer observations as authority.

What the demo must show

A payment fixture cannot become paid by changing its status. A changed target, expired approval, excess budget or repeated action is rejected. Uncertain remote completion goes to reconciliation.

Evidence required to advance
  • Both workflows retain their domain rules through the same durable core.
  • Destination idempotency or explicit reconciliation prevents unsafe automatic retries.
  • Reproducible decision pack: observed results, integration cost, proof status and unresolved production gates.

CROSS-SPRINT / DIFFICULT DEPENDENCY FIRST

Measure genuine admission.
Keep mocks visible.

Begin the membership and quota proof feasibility spike in Sprint 1. An attractive business demo cannot establish anonymous admission.

Compatibility before confidence

Check the chosen proof relation, identity commitments, field/hash, tree, class-credit bounds and EID binding against Midnight Registry requirements. Root changes and resealing must not renew quota. One proof combines the claims; library compatibility is an experiment.

Predeclared prototype gate

MPE-ECO-048 requires encoded slot roundUp64(104 + proofBytes) ≤ 4096 and a 10,000-proof verification benchmark on one core of a 4-vCPU VM. Report median and p99; adopt p99 ≤ 10 ms as conservative project policy.

The 4096-byte ceiling does not establish fit in the existing fixed 512-byte fixture slot. Actual relation and wire-profile evidence are required. These results have not been measured here.

AFTER THREE SPRINTS / INVESTMENT DECISION

Continue, revise or stop
with evidence.

What earns the next step

Independent formats agree; unsafe ambiguity rejects; process failures preserve the authorized outcome; new profiles reuse the core at an acceptable integration cost. Record commands, commits, toolchains, configuration, fixtures and complete fault results.

Compare turnaround and manual work with a participant baseline when available. Synthetic demos cannot establish customer savings.

What remains beyond the prototype

Finalized Registry integration, security review, replicated opaque retention, WAN/load evidence, operator economics and hardened operations. Automatic settlement needs separate business authority and anchored-message binding. OpenMLS and mobile discovery remain gated.

A broken recovery gate is repaired before adding breadth. An uncertain remote effect goes to reconciliation. Keep genuine-proof and mocked-workflow verdicts separate.
